checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in CA
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Occupancy load calc per IBC 1004 (mercantile = 60 sf gross/occupant for sales floor; 300 sf for stockroom)
Egress capacity sized to occupant load: 0.2 in/occupant for stairs, 0.15 in/occupant for level egress per IBC 1005
Accessible route from accessible entrance to all customer-accessible areas per ADA §206
ADA fixture counts per IBC Table 2902.1 (mercantile uses lower ratios — verify current edition)
Exterior signage permit (often a SEPARATE permit from the building TI — confirm with city sign code)
Fire alarm strobe coverage per NFPA 72 §18.5 (visible from any point, candela-rated to room area)
Sprinkler hydraulic recalc required if shelving / racking exceeds 12 ft (NFPA 13 §3.3.4 storage occupancy)
Storefront glazing: safety glazing per IBC 2406 for any pane within 24 in of door or 60 in of floor
Demising wall fire-rated per IBC 706.3 + STC ≥40 between tenants if not factory-built
Means of egress: ≥2 exits if occupant load >49 OR floor area >3,000 sf in M occupancy per IBC 1006
Public restroom availability per IBC 2902.3 (required for retail >150 occupants OR >300 ft from public restroom)
Energy code lighting + envelope per IECC C405 / C402 if HVAC or exterior wall is touched

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed commercial contractors pull the permits on the owner's behalf, and their CSLB license number must appear on the application. For this scope, the building contractor typically pulls the building permit, the C-10 electrical contractor pulls the electrical permit, and the C-36 plumbing contractor pulls the plumbing permit. The permit is still required even when licensed contractors are used.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Los Angeles City requires a CSLB license plus a Los Angeles City Business Tax Registration Certificate (BTRC). Contractors are commonly rejected at counter or online submission if the BTRC is missing or expired. Verify the BTRC is current before submitting any LADBS permit application.

common_mistakes: Submitting the TI without plan check documents for the new partition layout and restroom scope — commercial tenant improvements in LA are not simple over-the-counter jobs
Forgetting the Los Angeles City Business Tax Registration Certificate — LADBS can reject the application even if the CSLB license is valid
Assuming the electrical lighting work is covered by the building permit — lighting changes need the electrical permit too
Starting demolition or framing before the permit is issued and posted — LADBS can issue a stop-work order
Missing accessibility details for the restroom and storefront path of travel — this often triggers corrections during plan review
If the project is near a public street or sidewalk, not checking whether Bureau of Engineering review is also required before permit issuance
Skipping storefront/facade design review when windows, awnings, signs, or exterior finishes change.
Underestimating ADA path-of-travel upgrades for a primary-function retail alteration and missing the 20% cost allocation.
Submitting retail fixture plans without occupant-load, egress, aisle-width, and exit-sign/emergency-lighting coordination.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through LADBS online permit services at or via the permit status/inspection tools linked from LADBS. Phone: (213) 482-0000. Plan ahead for commercial work; book at least 24 hours in advance and expect longer lead times if the job is in a busy district or requires multiple trade inspections on the same day.

pro_tips: For Los Angeles commercial TI work, submit the building, electrical, and plumbing scope together so plan check can coordinate corrections in one cycle instead of three separate rounds
Have the contractor's CSLB license and LA City BTRC ready before opening the portal — missing registration is a common silent rejection
Include Title 24 energy forms with the lighting package up front; missing energy documentation is a frequent delay on commercial interiors
If the storefront door affects egress or accessibility, show clear door swing, hardware, and maneuvering clearances on the plan set to avoid correction cycles
If the site is near a street, curb, or sidewalk work area, check Bureau of Engineering requirements before you submit to LADBS
Coordinate the sign permit with the landlord's master sign program before ordering storefront signage.
Confirm retail parking ratio and accessible parking/path-of-travel scope before lease execution or final layout.
Package storefront elevations, glazing specs, awning details, and sign locations together so facade/design review does not lag the TI.

warnings: Commercial scope may require companion reviews/permits not fully proven here: electrical, mechanical, plumbing.
Some report claims do not yet have quoted source snippets; use the listed building department source before relying on them.
watch_out: Many cities require a Master Sign Program or landlord sign criteria approval before individual retail sign permits.
Parking, loading, and zoning variances commonly surface on change-of-use retail TIs and can block the certificate of occupancy.
Tenant leases often restrict facade, storefront, awning, penetrations, and signage even when code allows them — get landlord signoff early.
Illuminated signage may need both a sign permit and an electrical sign permit/inspection.
what_to_bring: Completed LADBS permit application and project address
Approved plan set for the tenant improvement, including floor plan, reflected ceiling plan, and restroom details
Contractor CSLB license number and Los Angeles City Business Tax Registration Certificate
Owner authorization letter or tenant authorization if the contractor is filing on behalf of the tenant
Equipment and fixture cut sheets for lighting, restroom fixtures, doors, and any accessibility hardware
Valuation breakdown for the $190,000 scope and any required Title 24 energy documentation
response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: For a commercial retail tenant improvement in downtown Los Angeles, zoning and historic overlay issues can still affect storefront changes, signage, and any exterior alterations. If the storefront door changes the exterior facade, check whether additional zoning, design review, or Bureau of Engineering approvals are needed. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for a retail TI, but lease and landlord approvals often are.
